On a match it appends a new empty list and `continue`s, so the separator is dropped. Otherwise it appends the token to `res[-1]`. Because a new list is opened at every separator, adjacent, leading and trailing separators produce empty partitions, and an empty input returns `[[]]`. The caller at raw.py:173 splits on `(OP, ';')` and sums `aux(sub)` over the parts. Review `aux` for how it handles empty sub-lists. The review should confirm that `token_values[:2]` works for both tuples and `TokenInfo` objects, and that logical-line counting stays correct when `;` is the last token. radon/complexity.py gets a brief check that it doesn't duplicate this logic. radon/metrics.py and radon/visitors.py get time to confirm they have no separate token-splitting path and to review how they consume the raw-metric results.

def _split_tokens(tokens, token, value):
    '''Split a list of tokens on the specified token pair (token, value),
    where *token* is the token type (i.e. its code) and *value* its actual
    value in the code.
    '''
    res = [[]]
    for token_values in tokens:
        if (token, value) == token_values[:2]:
            res.append([])
            continue
        res[-1].append(token_values)
    return res
